label: Richard N. Boyd, How to be a Moral Realist…: Moral judgments have a truth value: in practical…
locator: reprint §1.1, pp. 307–308: moral statements and truth
interpretation: Reuse the proposition that moral judgments are capable of truth and falsity. This does not add universal bivalence, infallibility or a necessary link to motivation. Both authors expressly distinguish realism from those stronger claims.
